refuted.evidence: AoN background-376's markdown/text really does end "You gain the Specialty Crafting skill feat." with no specialty, and the AoN mirror preserves such clauses elsewhere (merabite-prodigy "with alchemy", miner "with underground terrain", toymaker's 6-way list), so that part checks out — but the finding never looked at the second transcription that lives inside this repo: C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\.import-src\pf2e\packs\pf2e\backgrounds\alloysmith.json transcribes Rage of Elements p.44 as "...You gain the Specialty Crafting skill feat with the blacksmithing specialty." — word for word the sentence public/core-descriptions.json ships (ours matches Foundry's punctuation, not AoN's) — and backs it with a rule element `GrantItem ... preselectChoices {specialtyCrafting: blacksmithing}`. Foundry adds a preselect only where the printed text names the specialty (Merabite Prodigy=alchemy, Dendrologist=forest, Toymaker=a 6-option ChoiceSet, and nothing at all on the free granters Artisan/Tinker/Local Scion), so the clause is a rival reading of the book, not an invention of ours; and AoN's rendering of the same 10 Rage of Elements backgrounds is demonstrably non-verbatim in the same batch (Fire Warden: AoN says "Breath Control skill feat" for feat-5129/feat-763, which is a GENERAL feat, plus comma insertions Foundry lacks). Two conflicting transcriptions of one printed sentence is an owner question, not an askOwner:false deletion — and the fix as written ("strip the invented clause") would overwrite our own shipped spec text with AoN's.

askOwner.claim: WG auto-raises both past-life Lores to Expert at 3rd, Master at 7th and Legendary at 15th without consuming a skill increase, while print reads as a RESTRICTION on the skill increases the character already receives at those levels; ours models neither reading.
askOwner.printed: At 3rd level, 7th level, and 15th level, you receive skill increases, which you can apply only to these Lore skills.
askOwner.ours: No carrier at all — a field with no reader, and in fact no field. `skillIncreaseLevels` / `bonusSkillIncreaseLevels` (src/rules/types.ts:3303-3305) are CLASS chassis fields; nothing on `Background` adds a skill increase or constrains where one may be spent, and src/rules/restrictedSlots.ts is about spell slots only. grep 'reborn' across src returns only situationalBonuses.ts:3221.
askOwner.theirs: background id 836, three conditionals, each granting TWO Lore picks at a raised rank: `conditional  IF LEVEL GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUALS 3  IF LEVEL LESS_THAN 7  THEN  select title=Select a Lore optionsFilters={"group":"ADD-LORE","value":{"value":"E"}}` (x2); `IF LEVEL GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUALS 7  IF LEVEL LESS_THAN 15  THEN` the same at `"value":"M"` (x2); `IF LEVEL GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUALS 15  THEN` the same at `"value":"L"` (x2). Their character keeps its normal 3rd/7th/15th skill increases in addition.
askOwner.proposal: None — owner call. Adopting their encoding hands a Reborn Soul three free proficiency steps in two Lores on top of the character's normal skill increases, which is the opposite of what "you can apply only to these Lore skills" reads as; modelling the restriction instead needs a new lane (a per-level allow-list on the skill-increase picker) that nothing in the codebase has. I will not side against print by adopting theirs.
askOwner.evidence: Their id 836 does carry three level-gated conditionals (>=3 & <7 → two ADD-LORE selects at "E"; >=7 & <15 → "M"; >=15 → "L"), granted alongside the character's ordinary increases; on our side grep 'reborn' over src/ returns only situationalBonuses.ts:3221 (the +1/stupefied clause), `skillIncreaseLevels`/`bonusSkillIncreaseLevels` are read only as `cls?.skillIncreaseLevels` (build.ts:2996, :8190, :8385) so they are class chassis, and restrictedSlots.ts is spell slots only — no carrier for either reading. Print's "you receive skill increases, which you can apply only to these Lore skills" is genuinely ambiguous between a grant and a restriction, so askOwner is right.
